thread:
maria: fyi — customer ACME / support ticket 8921 reporting large p99 increase from eu-west starting ~04:10 UTC. They see overall API p99 go from ~2.3s -> ~8s, and in traces the TLS handshake portion is huge. forwarding dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/requests?probe=eu-west&span=tls_handshake :rotating_light:
inc-bot: [ALERT] route:eu-west p99 /v1/generate = 8.1s (sustained 12m) :rotating_light:
devon: oncall here, thanks maria. can you paste one example request id and a short curl timing from the customer side? also newrelic link?
maria: customer-probe-id=acme-8921-20260310, attaching curl from their side (they ran from eu-west client):
```
$ curl -w "time_namelookup:%{time_namelookup} time_connect:%{time_connect} time_appconnect:%{time_appconnect} time_starttransfer:%{time_starttransfer} time_total:%{time_total}\n" -o /dev/null -s https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
time_namelookup:0.008 time_connect:0.020 time_appconnect:6.102 time_starttransfer:6.180 time_total:6.185
```
maria: they also attached a quick traceroute from their host — shows a hop detour through a non-eu-west POP (looks like eu-central bounce).
alan: ok interesting — large gap is between connect and appconnect, that's TLS handshake. appconnect=6.1s. that smells like cross-pop or upstream peer causing extra RTTs or packet loss leading to handshake retries.
alan: maria, can you paste DNS resolution for api.redwood.example from the customer host (dig +trace) and our edge egress metrics for that timeframe?
maria: dig output they gave: `api.redwood.example. 60 IN A 3.7.21.45` (one IP). dig +trace to the IP shows GSLB returned eu-central weight earlier at ~04:08 for that ASN.
devon: running quick openssl test from our eu-west pop (eu-west-1-pop-3):
```
$ openssl s_time -connect 3.7.21.45:443 -new
# handshake times (sample): 0.05s, 0.06s, 6.0s, 0.04s
```
devon: see those outliers — intermittent long handshakes from eu-west -> that IP. packet captures show retransmits during handshake on some connections.
alan: sounds like upstream peer intermittently blackholing or queueing. possibilities: (1) GSLB handed traffic to an overloaded upstream or (2) peering ISPs shifting path -> cross-zone hop. do we have a recent GSLB weight change or BGP announcement?
lina: we rolled a small GSLB weight tweak at 04:05 for canary traffic (internal change #GSLB-2026-03-10) — rolling back now to confirm.
alan: rollback good idea. in parallel, do a temporary route override for the affected IP to steer egress to eu-central pop for ACME CID. command: `rbctl route override add --cidr 18.33.0.0/24 --from-pop eu-west-1-pop-3 --to-pop eu-central-1-pop-1 --reason "mitigate tls tail p99"`
devon: adding override for ACME CID + applying temporary TLS session cache relaxation on eu-west to reduce handshake retries: `edgectl config set pop eu-west-1-pop-3 tls_session_timeout 120s` (note: small risk to memory).
maria: applied rollback of GSLB change at 04:22, applied route override at 04:24. customer reports immediate improvement: p99 dropped to ~1.1s within two minutes.
inc-bot: [UPDATE] route:eu-west p99 /v1/generate -> 1.1s (after overrides).
devon: can we capture a full tcpdump of a failing handshake and a healthy handshake for postmortem? capture saved to s3://redwood-debug/eu-west/1718601234-handshake-pcap.pcap
alan: I'll open a peering ticket with provider (ticket PEER-4477) including tcpdump + BGP adj logs. preliminary hypothesis: intermittent queuing on upstream next-hop caused TCP retransmit during TLS ClientHello -> ServerHello, resulting in handshake timeout and TCP recovery.
lina: follow-up actions: 1) revert route override once peering confirms fix and p99 stable for 30m; 2) add alert rule that specifically tracks `span:tls_handshake` > 3s at p99; 3) document mitigation steps in runbook (add `rbctl route override` snippet).
customer-success: I'll relay to ACME that we've mitigated and we're working with upstream. they asked for a short RCA and ETA.
devon: assigning postmortem owners: alan (networking) + lina (prodops) + maria (customer comms). timeline note: root cause likely upstream peering pathing + an unfortunate GSLB weight nudge that sent traffic to the affected IP. mitigation sequence recorded.
maria: customer confirmed degraded calls stopped at ~04:26 and are happy with provisional fix. I'll keep thread open until peering confirms and we revert override.
alan: opened peering ticket and included BGP dumps, provider acknowledged and scheduled a route flap check.
inc-bot: [RESOLUTION CHECK] p99 stable <1.5s for 25m — consider closing.
maria: closing in 30m unless anything new. thanks all :thumbsup:
